newsitem.title: USA: Reprieve for Nicaraguans facing U.S. deportation.
newsitem.headline: Reprieve for Nicaraguans facing U.S. deportation.

text.p: A Miami judge extended for a further 10 working days an injunction blocking any mass deportations of Nicaraguans from the United States, legal officials said on Wednesday.

The reprieve gives hope to an estimated 40,000 Nicaraguans in the Miami area, most of them longtime residents, who are under threat of being kicked out of the United States under tough new immigration rules.
Judge James King on Tuesday ordered that hearings on their immigration status should go on until June 12. In the meantime the Immigration and Naturalisation Service is barred from deporting anyone.

A lawsuit filed on the Nicaraguans' behalf charges that the United States allowed them to work and pay taxes for years before bringing in new provisions denying them a chance to apply for permanent residency. Under the new laws they can be summarily deported.
"I think its just fair to let people have a hearing somewhere," King said.
Issuing his original May 14 injunction, King said that deporting so many Nicaraguans would unfairly split up families who have made good and honest lives in the United States.
The new INS provisions also affect Salvadorans, Haitians , Guatemalans and other groups.
